source: Pitt (2020) Mental Representation, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
finding: Lists the rival theories of content: causal-informational, teleosemantic, asymmetric dependency, conceptual role (holist, molecular, atomist), resemblance, phenomenal intentionality. Each has a standard objection.
numbers: Entry first published 2000, revised 21 Jan 2020. No empirical effect sizes.
quote: Such relations are common, but representation is not.
limits: Philosophical, not empirical. The page was read through a fetch tool summary, not the raw full text.
agent_relevance: No theory is settled, so the agent should not bet on one account of what a representation 'means'. Judge representations by what they let the agent do and check.

source: Pitt (2020) SEP, section on informational theories
finding: Plain causal covariation is too weak. Tree trunks, smoke and thermostats carry information but do not represent. Mental tokens can be caused by things they do not represent, and can represent things that never caused them (the error or disjunction worry).
numbers: Examples: tree trunks, smoke, thermostat.
limits: The error problem is the main reason teleosemantic and asymmetric-dependency views exist.
agent_relevance: A feature that merely correlates with an answer is not a good representation. In probing terms, decodable is not the same as used.

source: Pitt (2020) SEP, section on imagery debate
finding: 1970s response-time studies found mental manipulation times vary with size and orientation of the imagined figure. Kosslyn read this as pictorial format; Pylyshyn argued propositional explanations fit as well.
numbers: Qualitative summary; no N given in the entry.
limits: Classic case where the same data fit two formats. Format was not settled by behaviour alone.
agent_relevance: The same output can come from different internal formats. Format questions (S2) need a discriminating test, not one accuracy score.

source: Li et al. (2023) Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task (Othello-GPT)
finding: GPT trained only on Othello move strings predicts legal moves and holds a board state that nonlinear probes can read and interventions can change.
numbers: Illegal top-1 move rate: 0.01% (synthetic data), 5.17% (championship data), 93.29% (untrained). Linear probe error never below 20% (synthetic best 20.4%, randomized net 25 to 26%). Two-layer MLP probe error: synthetic 1.7% at best layer, championship 9.4%, randomized about 25.5%.
limits: One toy domain with fully known rules. Synthetic data was random legal play, so it covers the game tree widely. Championship data gave weaker results.
agent_relevance: Strongest early case that next-token training can build an internal model of a hidden state. It still needed a causal check, which it supplied with interventions.

source: Nanda, Lee, Wattenberg (2023) Emergent Linear Representations in World Models of Self-Supervised Sequence Models
finding: Follow-up to Li et al. shows the board is linearly encoded, but as MINE/YOURS (relative to the player to move), not BLACK/WHITE. Li et al.'s 'linear probes fail' result was a coordinate-frame problem.
numbers: Linear probe accuracy MINE/YOURS/EMPTY: 90.9% at layer 1 rising to 99.5% at layer 8. Intervention errors (flipping colours): null baseline 2.72 wrong tiles, nonlinear (Li) 0.12, linear probe addition 0.10; erasing: 2.73, 0.11, 0.02.
limits: Still Othello only. The right encoding was found only after choosing a better coordinate frame.
agent_relevance: The format of a good internal representation can be player-relative, not absolute. When designing state, the frame (relative to the actor) may matter more than probe power.

source: Hazineh, Zhang, Chiu (2023) Linear Latent World Models in Simple Transformers: A Case Study on Othello-GPT
finding: Independently finds linear board probes work in Othello-GPT, even with a 1-layer model, once labels are MINE/YOURS.
numbers: Linear probe accuracy BLACK/WHITE about 75% across layers; MINE/YOURS 90.8% at layer 1 to 99.5% at layer 8 (Table 1).
limits: Same toy game. Independent replication of Nanda et al., not a new domain.
agent_relevance: Two groups agree, so the linear world-state result in this domain is solid.

source: Karvonen (2024) Emergent World Models and Latent Variable Estimation in Chess-Playing Language Models
finding: Extends Othello result to chess with real human games and linear probes. Board state and a hidden skill-level variable are linearly readable and the board vector can be edited.
numbers: Best square-state probe 99.6% (16 layer), 99.1% (8 layer); randomized nets 74.7% and 75.0%. Skill probe 90.5% vs 69.3% random. Legal move rate on edited board: 40.5% without intervention, 92.0% with (16 layer; 8 layer 41.0% to 90.4%). Unedited board 99.9% vs 85.4% with intervention. Model won 46% (8L) and 64% (16L) of games vs Stockfish level 0. 5,000 test cases.
limits: Best intervention success is 92%, not 100%, so the representation is not the only route to the move. Randomized-net baseline is already about 75% because most squares are empty.
agent_relevance: Real-world data suffice. A tracked latent variable (player skill) can also sit in the state, so the agent's state may encode who it is modelling, not only the world.

source: Vafa, Chen, Rambachan, Kleinberg, Mullainathan (2024) Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
finding: Next-token accuracy and probes are not enough. Defines compression (same state should give same continuations) and distinction (different states should give different ones). Transformers fail compression on city navigation even when standard tests look near perfect.
numbers: Navigation: next-token accuracy about 1.00 and current-state probe 0.91 to 0.99, but compression precision 0.05 to 0.50 and distinction recall 0.35 to 0.99 depending on training data (shortest paths vs random walks). Untrained net near 0. Seat-order logic puzzle: task accuracy 0.83 to 1.00 but compression 0.08 to 0.53 across Llama-2/3, Mixtral, Qwen, GPT-3.5/4; no model above 40% compression precision, distinction recall at most 0.60.
limits: Tested on deterministic finite automata. Task accuracy can hide an incoherent state map. Training on random walks (more diverse) helped.
agent_relevance: Direct test for G3: check a representation on things it was not fitted to. A model that answers correctly may not keep one state per situation, so the agent should canonicalise state in code.

source: Gurnee and Tegmark (2024) Language Models Represent Space and Time
finding: Linear probes on Llama-2 activations recover real-world latitude/longitude and event dates.
numbers: Out-of-sample R2 at 60% depth, Llama-2 7B/13B/70B: World 0.881/0.896/0.911, USA 0.799/0.825/0.864, NYC 0.219/0.237/0.359, Historical 0.785/0.804/0.835, Entertainment 0.788/0.806/0.885, Headlines 0.564/0.645/0.746. Nonlinear MLP probes add little.
limits: Probes are trained on the activations, so some R2 is probe work; paper adds prompt and ablation checks. NYC (obscure entities) is weakest and gains most from scale. Table row order for 7B/13B/70B was matched from the printed table and may be slightly off.
agent_relevance: Continuous quantities appear linearly decodable, and quality rises with scale. For a small model expect poor structure on obscure entities.

source: Marks and Tegmark (2024) The Geometry of Truth
finding: At sufficient scale LLaMA-2 linearly represents whether a statement is true. Probes generalise across datasets, and mass-mean probes are more causally implicated than logistic ones.
numbers: Probes trained on larger_than plus smaller_than exceed 95% on Spanish-English translation (13B and 70B). Intervention normalised indirect effects, LLaMA-2-70B: MM false-to-true 0.55, true-to-false 0.99 (cities+neg_cities); 13B MM 0.13 and 0.19. Probes trained on 'likely' text do worse than chance where probability and truth anti-correlate.
limits: Simple curated true/false datasets. Negation generalisation fails without negated training data. 7B generalises poorly. Table cell alignment was partly garbled in extraction.
agent_relevance: Supports a truth direction in large models, but weak at small scale and can track plausibility. Do not use a probe as a verifier (G2/G3); use code checks.

source: Burns, Ye, Klein, Steinhardt (2022) Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
finding: Contrast-Consistent Search finds a truth-like direction with no labels, beating zero-shot and less prompt-sensitive.
numbers: About 4% above zero-shot on average over 10 QA datasets and 6 models. Table 1 (one model row read): CCS 62.1 to 84.8 per model against a logistic-regression ceiling of 79.8 to 90.5.
limits: T0 trained on 9 of the 10 datasets, so excluded from averages. Later failed under adversarial prompts (see Farquhar).
agent_relevance: First claim that representation is recoverable without labels. Not a basis for trusting the model's own beliefs.

source: Farquhar et al. (2023) Challenges with unsupervised LLM knowledge discovery
finding: Refutes the key claim: CCS, PCA and K-means find the most prominent feature, not knowledge. Proves arbitrary features satisfy the CCS consistency loss.
numbers: With Banana/Shed prompt insertion, ground-truth accuracy fell to 50% (chance) for all unsupervised methods; CCS was bimodal across random seeds, some at 100% on the distractor. With 'Alice thinks...' inserted, methods tracked Alice's opinion, not truth. Topic-confound set (50% about company): nearly half of CCS seeds predicted Alice's opinion.
limits: Chinchilla70B and T5-FLAN-XXL with constructed distractors. Authors expect the identification problem to persist for other unsupervised methods.
agent_relevance: Strong failed replication. The agent cannot read what the model believes from activations without labels. One more reason to use checked outputs, not self-report.

source: Levinstein and Herrmann (2023) Still no lie detector for language models (cited in Marks and Tegmark and in Farquhar et al.)
finding: As cited in two papers read: truth probes fail to generalise in basic ways, such as to negated statements. Marks and Tegmark respond that training on statements plus their opposites fixes much of this.
numbers: Not read directly; no numbers recorded.
limits: Secondary citation only.
agent_relevance: Treat probe generalisation as dependent on training data design.

source: Belinkov (2022) Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
finding: Reviews probing. Main problem: high probe accuracy shows information is decodable, not that the model uses it. Proposes controls (control tasks, random baselines, control functions) and causal methods.
numbers: No single effect size; survey of control designs (selectivity, information gain vs control function).
limits: A squib; no new experiments.
agent_relevance: Decodable is not used. A good representation test is causal: edit it and watch behaviour.

source: Hewitt and Liang (2019) Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
finding: A probe that is too expressive can learn the task itself. Introduces control tasks (random labels per word type) and selectivity = task accuracy minus control accuracy.
numbers: POS tagging, MLP probe: 97.3% accuracy but 92.8% control, selectivity 4.5. Linear probe: 97.2% accuracy, 71.2% control, selectivity 26.0. ELMo layer 1 vs 2: accuracy 97.2 vs 96.6 but selectivity 26.0 vs 31.4. Small hidden size (10), weight decay and small training sets raise selectivity.
limits: English POS tagging and dependency edges on ELMo-type representations.
agent_relevance: Always report a control when claiming a representation holds something. Compare probe power, not only accuracy. The Othello nonlinear vs linear debate is a direct case.

source: Abdou et al. (2021) Can Language Models Encode Perceptual Structure Without Grounding? A Case Study in Color
finding: Text-only LMs (BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA and others) align with CIELAB colour space. Alignment is stronger for larger models and for warm colours.
numbers: RSA Kendall tau significant in all configurations; PMI baselines RSA 0.11 to 0.17 and fastText 0.23; linear-map selectivity about 0.70 to 0.72 for baselines; 0.4 of CIELAB variance explained by about 10 dimensions and 0.7 by 30 to 40; shuffled-centroid control gives non-significant RSA.
limits: Colour has few terms (small N) and strong distributional cues. Part of the signal is learnable by simple PMI models, so it does not show deep grounding.
agent_relevance: Perceptual structure is partly recoverable from text alone. But part is simple co-occurrence.

source: Huh, Cheung, Wang, Isola (2024) The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
finding: Claims representations from different models and modalities converge (mutual nearest-neighbour alignment) as models grow more capable.
numbers: Alignment rises with VTAB task performance; language-vision alignment tracks LM score; more descriptive captions (DCI 1 to 30+ words) raise alignment with vision.
limits: Authors list limits: robotics lacks a standard state representation; alignment values are low in absolute terms (about 0.1 to 0.2 in plots); sensory and modality-specific information may not converge; correlational.
agent_relevance: If representations converge toward the structure of the world, a good representation preserves relational structure (a structuralist view). Suggests an agent can borrow structure across modalities, but the evidence is correlational.

source: Bender and Koller (2020) Climbing towards NLU: On Meaning, Form, and Understanding in the Age of Data
finding: Position paper: a system trained only on form cannot in principle learn meaning, defined as the relation between form and communicative intent (octopus thought experiment).
numbers: Argument only; no experiments.
quote: a system trained only on form has a priori no way to learn meaning
limits: Contested. Rival view is conceptual role (Piantadosi and Hill). Later results (colour, space, Othello) show form-only training yields structured internal models, though not proof of meaning.
agent_relevance: Frames the debate that later empirical papers test. Do not assume text-only means no world structure.

source: Piantadosi and Hill (2022) Meaning without reference in large language models
finding: Argues LLMs plausibly capture meaning via conceptual role (Block 1998), because reference does not fix concepts (postage stamp, Frege, Wittgenstein examples). Meaning is fixed by relations among internal states.
numbers: Argument paper; no experiments.
quote: meaning cannot be determined from a model's architecture, training data, or objective function
limits: Conceptual-role views face holism and solipsism objections (SEP). Philosophical.
agent_relevance: Supports judging representations by internal relations and consistency, which code can check. Rival to the grounding view.

source: Mitchell and Krakauer (2023) The Debate Over Understanding in AI's Large Language Models
finding: Surveys the split over whether LLMs understand; cites a 2022 survey of NLP researchers showing an even split.
numbers: 480 respondents; 51% agreed a text-only model could understand language in some non-trivial sense, 49% disagreed.
limits: Opinion survey of one community in 2022, not a measure of any model.
agent_relevance: No field agreement, so treat understanding as a testable property of the agent, not an assumption.

source: Millière and Buckner (2024) A Philosophical Introduction to Language Models Part II: The Way Forward
finding: Reviews probing, attribution and causal intervention. Probe success does not show the feature plays a causal role. Argues for interventionist evidence for representational claims.
numbers: Review; no new numbers.
limits: Philosophy-of-science framing, mostly qualitative. Opened by keyword scan of the extracted text, not read in full.
agent_relevance: Use causal intervention tests, not only probes, before calling a state a representation.

source: Yildirim and Paul (2023) From Word Models to World Models: Translating from Natural Language to the Probabilistic Language of Thought
finding: Downloaded but not read in detail. Proposes LLMs translate language into probabilistic programs that carry world models.
numbers: No figures recorded.
limits: Not read; do not rely on it.
agent_relevance: Possible link: separate language from the world model that reasons.

source: Marks and Tegmark (2024) The Geometry of Truth, generalisation section
finding: Probe generalisation improves with model scale and when training includes statements and their opposites; the negation failure reported by others shrinks.
numbers: Training on cities plus neg_cities fixes generalisation to negated translation statements; larger_than plus smaller_than improves results even though structurally different; 13B and 70B generalise highly, 7B less so; mass-mean probes underperform logistic and CCS probes at 7B but match them at 13B and 70B.
limits: Only simple true/false datasets of the authors; not open-ended claims.
agent_relevance: Representations of truth are scale-dependent. A small agent model should not be expected to have a clean truth feature.

source: Li et al. (2023) Othello-GPT, layer and baseline results
finding: Probe accuracy peaks in the middle layers and falls toward the output. A randomized network also scores above chance on probes, so a random baseline is required.
numbers: Randomized-net nonlinear probe error about 25.5 to 26.4% across layers; best constant guess (all empty) about 47% error (53% in main text); trained synthetic model 1.7% at layer 7.
limits: Single game; gap between trained and random is what carries the claim.
agent_relevance: Report a random-weights baseline for every probing claim.
